claim_being_audited: The actor claims the current record is sufficient to certify the model for launch despite a documented unresolved advertising-policy weakness, because aggregate readiness is above threshold, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and governance guidance supports managed-risk deployment with monitoring and disclosures.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows no material weakness remains or shows an approved mitigation satisfying all required fields.
Treat aggregate readiness and rehearsal outcomes as supportive but not sufficient when a policy-required disclosure or approval predicate remains unresolved.
Discount generalized external governance guidance as secondary context rather than dispositive support for an internal certification decision.
Because evidence access is actor-summary-only, unresolved predicates and overclaims should weigh against a clean compliance finding.
evidence_requests: Provide the underlying admissible evidence showing whether the advertising-policy weakness was formally determined not to be material.
Provide an approved mitigation or risk acceptance record containing owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion.
Provide the actual model-card draft and reviewer comments to verify whether the disclosure statement conflicts with the known weakness.
Provide the underlying policy note or approval record showing certification is permitted with this exact unresolved condition.
specific_concerns: The policy text requires either evidence that no material weakness remains or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion for certification without material caveats.
The actor's own summary says the mitigation artifact is still a draft and lacks at least an owner and alert threshold, which leaves the policy predicate unresolved.

The model-card disclosure issue appears live because the record reportedly says there are no known material limitations while a reviewer flagged possible disclosure of the advertising-policy weakness.
Public governance guidance about documentation and monitoring is not equivalent to internal approval of an unresolved material weakness.
unsupported_claims: That the locked certification decision is affirmatively supportable on the present admissible record without first resolving the disclosure/approval gap.
That draft monitoring and a draft runbook meaningfully cure the current disclosure requirement under the stated release policy.
Any implication that aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one incidents are sufficient by themselves to satisfy the certification standard when a material weakness may remain unresolved.
